findings.title: Deposit is within the amount cap
findings.detail: This amount check does not verify deposit protection or authenticity. Annual rent GBP 15600; cap = 15600 / 52 * 5 (GBP 1500.00 rounded down to pennies); requested GBP 1500. Importance: 85/100. Conditional: Confirm that the rented property is in England. Confirm this is an ordinary private tenancy, not an excluded arrangement. Confirm that rent and deposit cover the same whole tenancy. The amount arithmetic stands: GBP 1300 x 12 = GBP 15,600 a year, which is below GBP 50,000, so the cap is five weeks' rent (15,600 / 52 x 5 = GBP 1,500.00). The stated deposit of GBP 1,500 is exactly at the cap, not above it, so this is a correctly limited amount-cap pass. However, the contract text does not establish that the property is in England (jurisdiction is unknown), that this is an ordinary private tenancy outside excluded arrangements, or that the rent and deposit relate to the same whole tenancy. Nothing in the contract defeats the calculation, so dismissal is not warranted. Compliance with the amount cap says nothing about deposit protection or authenticity. Sources: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/tenant-fees-act-2019-guidance-for-tenants
